text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose modestly today, continuing a sharp rebound from its 6.76% drop over the past two weeks. The recovery aligns with tightening fuel supply dynamics: heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year ahead of winter, and diesel & heating oil inventories at 103.33 million barrels remain relatively lean, supporting margin conditions for refiners who produce these products. Refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, near full tilt, which positions Marathon to capture value from the supply-demand mismatch as demand heads into the cold season.

The broader headwind—Russian crude production rebounding to 8.73 million barrels per day, pushing global markets into surplus—explains why the stock fell hard earlier in the month. But the winter fuel crunch and strong operating rates suggest refiners can still earn solid margins even in a surplus crude environment, which is why the stock has stabilized and edged higher over the past few days.
